unit.title: CRO priority order: clarity/hierarchy, copy, offer, proof, friction

claim.text: The source ranks conversion-rate optimization elements in order: clarity and hierarchy (instant understanding and above the fold), copy (removes doubt and speaks to desire), offer (worth converting on), proof (belief in claims and unique mechanism), and friction (anything physically in the way of purchase).
claim.quote: First is clarity and hierarchy. The key here is can the user clearly understand it instantly and is it above the fold. Number two is copy. Does it remove doubt and speak to the actual desire? Number three is the offer. Is the thing on offer actually worth converting on? How good is the offer? Number four is proof. Do they actually believe you and the claims that you're saying and the unique mechanism? And the number five is friction. Is there anything physically in the way of the purchase?
